parts.label: Early vote
why: Registered Democrats cast 69% of the 357,650 ballots in Maryland so far, against 15% for the other party.
That is 2.9 points worse for Democrats than the forecast expected by now.
Statewide numbers; this weighs less for a House race.

parts.label: National tide
why: Gallup party identification moved from Republicans 48 Democrats 45 in the third quarter of 2024 to Democrats 50 Republicans 39 in the third quarter of 2026, 14 points toward the Democrats.
This district moves 1.81 points for every point the nation moves, so it feels about 25.3 points of that tide, a tailwind for Glenn Ivey.

D.t: Glenn Ivey leads by 83.8 in the forecast and wins 100% of simulations. The cushion is about 244,941 votes; a one point swing is about 1,462 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +80.6 and D +86.6. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
